en: A vector database is a special kind of
database which you can run on your system or
on some server your company may be renting.
And it's a database that, like all
databases, stores data, but it stores data
converted to so-called vector embeddings,
which are simply numeric representations of
the data, of the text, for example, that
should be stored there.
Let's say, the text extracted from PDF
documents, which should make up your
knowledge base.
And those text extractions are converted to
those vector embeddings to basically
represent how that text is related to other
pieces of text. Now, that clearly sounds
very abstract, and the details indeed are
not important unless you're developing such
a vector database. But the idea is that you
find a way of numerically representing how
text is related to each other.
And being able to store that representation
in a database.
That numeric representation then makes it
easier to search that text and to search for
text that's related to your prompt when
you're sending a prompt to a large language
model. Because in order to
ground the response in your
knowledge database, for example,
if you want to use such a RAG approach as
explained, you must find knowledge entries
entries in your database, in your vector
database, that are related to your prompt
you're about to send to the large language
model.
Therefore, what a vector database does is it
offers tools, you could say, that allow you
to convert your prompt to the same kind of
numerical vector representation as the data
stored in the database, and then find
relevant entries in that database that are
related to the prompt that is that is about
to be sent to the large language model. And
then those related entries are converted
back to text, so to say, and the actual text
is injected into your prompt. And then the
combined prompt plus the relevant sources
can be sent to the large language model.
That's how this RAG approach works, as you
learned. And under the hood, it works with
help of a vector database, which uses this
numerical representation of text, which is
used to represent how different pieces of
text are related to each other. That's the
high-level overview, which is the only thing
that matters here. But that's why vector
databases are quite important when building
RAG systems, which in turn can be a useful
way of grounding your responses in actual
sources, specifically, typically in
knowledge databases you may be maintaining
in your company.
